title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). Th. 4 is an equivalence of categories between two kinds of data. (a) Triples (X,K,S): X is a compact conformal (Riemann) surface with boundary, and (K,S) is a compact 1-dimensional complex with ∂X ⊂ K ⊂ X and suitable regularity (piecewise 'rectifiable'). (b) Systems (X̃, S̃, σ): X̃ is the compact bordered surface obtained by cutting X open along K, S̃ is a finite subset of ∂X̃, and σ is a regular involution on Déc(∂X̃/S̃), i.e. on the pieces of the boundary cut at S̃. The functor (a)→(b) is cutting along K (Th. 3 and Lemma 2). For the inverse functor (b)→(a), the topological gluing X = X̃/R is clear. Grothendieck defines the conformal structure sheaf on X as the continuous functions that are holomorphic on X∖K ≅ X̃∖∂X̃.

This page. He notes the key point: one must check that this sheaf really is a conformal structure with boundary in which K sits, and that cutting along K automatically gives back the original structure on X̃. Since this is local, he says it is equivalent to two model cases, collected as 'Lemme 3 (cas particuliers)'. A first, crossed-out formulation tried to construct directly a closed arc K in the half-disc H∩D°, with an endpoint on the boundary, splitting H∩D° into two components U', U''.

(a) Welding two copies of the half-disc H along the boundary segment [0,1] via a rectifiable homeomorphism σ:[0,1]→[0,1], regular near 0. Locally this models a point of the welded seam, with 0 lying on the boundary of X. A variant welds along [-1,1] via σ:[-1,1]→[-1,1], regular near 0. Here 0 is an interior point of an edge of K, or a vertex where K meets ∂X.

(b) On the next page: folding the closed half-disc onto itself via an involution [0,1]→[-1,0] with σ(0)=0, regular near 0. This models a terminal vertex of K (the end of a slit). With σ(x) = -x the chart is z ↦ z².

In modern terms, the page reduces the gluing half of a 'cut-and-paste along embedded graphs' equivalence to local conformal welding statements. These are existence of a chart that is a homeomorphism and holomorphic off the seam, plus the requirement that the seam be conformally removable, so the structure is unique and restricts back to X̃. The purpose is a rigorous surgery calculus for Riemann surfaces with embedded graphs, in the 1983–84 setting of dessins and maps on surfaces.
errors: The regularity hypothesis 'rectifiable' is not the right condition for conformal welding. Grothendieck himself hesitates: '(au plus régulier que ça ?)'.

If 'rectifiable' means merely of bounded variation or absolutely continuous, welding may fail to exist or be non-unique. The standard sufficient condition is quasisymmetry (Pfluger, Lehto–Virtanen), with uniqueness coming from removability of quasiarcs. Bi-Lipschitz or piecewise real-analytic σ would suffice.

For uniqueness ('qui automatiquement redonne la structure de X̃'), the welded seam must be conformally removable. This is not automatic for an arbitrary homeomorphism, and the page does not address it.

The reduction from the global statement to the local cases is sound, since conformal structure is a local notion. Corner and endpoint behaviour at 0 needs the extra 'régulier au voisinage de 0' hypothesis, which he correctly flags.

ideas.what: Defining the conformal structure on a glued surface as the continuous functions that are holomorphic off the seam K
ideas.modern_name: Conformal welding / removable sets for the welded curve
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pfluger (1960), Lehto–Virtanen (1960s); later Bishop, Astala–Jones–Kupiainen–Saksman, Sheffield

ideas.what: Reduction of the welding problem along a graph to two local model cases: two half-discs welded along an interval with an endpoint on the boundary, and a half-disc folded onto itself (slit endpoint)
ideas.modern_name: Local welding models at edges and degree-1 vertices of an embedded graph
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard folklore in cut-and-paste of Riemann surfaces

ideas.what: Equivalence between (surface, embedded graph containing the boundary) and (cut surface, gluing involution on boundary arcs)
ideas.modern_name: Cut-and-paste / ribbon-graph style description of Riemann surfaces with embedded graphs
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Poincaré); in dessin context Grothendieck's Esquisse (1984); later Strebel, Penner, Kontsevich in other forms
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to 'chirurgie' of conformal surfaces, but not to this categorical statement

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates a categorical cut-and-paste equivalence for bordered Riemann surfaces along arbitrary compact graphs, with 'rectifiable' gluing data. He leaves the analytic regularity condition open. The right answer is quasisymmetric gluing plus removability, which was available in the welding literature but which he apparently did not use.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a clean functorial formulation of welding along graphs, including boundary and endpoint cases. It is close in spirit to Bishop's welding methods for 'true trees'/dessins. However, the analytic content is known, so the novelty is mostly in framing.

deep.surprise_reason: The page reduces the gluing functor of a cut-and-paste equivalence to local conformal welding cases. This is mathematically standard, known since the 1960s, and stated with a non-optimal regularity hypothesis. It is historically interesting as Grothendieck's own route to welding in his dessins period, but contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: The insertion read as '(deux cas plaires [?])' is better read as '(deux exemplaires)'. It refers to two copies of H.
'Recollement de H : H' should read 'Recollement de H à H'. The point is gluing two copies of the half-disc.
In the crossed-out Lemma 3: 'K est un intervalle ... d'extrémité o, qui partage H∩D° en deux comp. connexes U', U''' (an arc with endpoint 0 splitting the half-disc).
The first sentence plausibly reads 'qui automatiquement redonne naissance à la structure conforme à bord X̃ de départ'. 'naissance' is struck or uncertain.
